SOCIO ECONOMIC SURVEY 2023-24

SOCIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

5,512 Health Camps have been conducted in tribal areas
where 14,39,914 beneficiaries were screened and 11,714
patients were referred.

During 2023-24, under Dr NTR Vaidya Seva Scheme
13,22,319 number of patients benefited with preauthori-
sed amount of Rs. 3762.06 Crores. District wise data of Dr
NTR Vaidya Seva from 01.04.2023 to 31.03.2024 is
annexed as Annexure 8.11.

## Employees Health Scheme

The scheme was introduced to benefit state government
employees, pensioners, and their dependents, with the
premium contribution shared equally (50:50) between
the state government and the employees/pensioners.
Under this scheme, 2,510 medical procedures have been
approved, along with treatment for 25 identified chronic
diseases. Additionally, 170 procedures have been
designated for follow-up treatments. The coverage limit
is set at Rs. 2.00 lakhs per episode of illness, with no
restrictions on the number of episodes. Outpatient
treatment for the 25 identified chronic diseases is
provided in government facilities. The trust has issued
176 Letters of Credit (LOCs) to hospitals for cashless
treatment of high-end procedures, such as liver
transplants, heart transplants, bone marrow transplants,
and deep brain stimulation, amounting to Rs. 25.23
crores, based on the recommendations of the technical
committee established by the government.

The total number of beneficiaries covered under the
scheme is 2,214,509, which includes 510,740 state
government employees and 298,912 pensioners.
Additionally, the dependents of government employees
and pensioners covered under the scheme total
1,404,857.

During the 2023-24 period, under the Employee Health
Scheme (EHS), 119,761 employees and pensioners
benefited from a pre-authorized amount of Rs. 400.70
crores.

## Working Journalists Health Scheme

The government has introduced the Working Journalists
Health Scheme to provide free healthcare services,
similar to the Employee Health Scheme (EHS), for
accredited journalists identified by the Information and
Public Relations (I&PR) Department, the nodal agency for

this initiative. The annual premium for each journalist is
set at Rs. 2,500, which amounts to Rs. 208 per month. The
premium payment is shared equally, with both the
government and the journalists contributing 50% each.
In accordance with the government’s renewal orders, the
scheme is administered by the Trust for Working
Journalists in the state. Currently, the scheme benefits
13,000 working journalists and 45,000 dependents of
those enrolled in the program. During the 2023-24
period, 725 journalists received assistance under this
scheme, with a total pre-authorized amount of Rs. 1.63
crores.

## Amaravati Residents Health Scheme

The residents (both white card and pink card holders)
within the Amaravathi area who are residing as on
08.12.2014 shall be provided free medical facilities
subject to certain conditions Accordingly, the Trust is
providing services to the residents of CRDA region
covering 38,120 families on the guidelines of Dr NTR
Vaidya Seva Scheme. CRDA provides the requisite
budget for the beneficiaries those who are not covered
under Dr. NTR Vaidya Seva Scheme. Health Cards had
been distributed to 1,06,496 Amaravati Residents
(Health Scheme beneficiaries) till 2019 and further no
health cards have been distributed till now.

## Aarogya Raksha

The Aarogya Raksha Scheme has been implemented for
families above the poverty line as part of the Dr. NTR
Vaidya Seva Scheme from April 7, 2017. It requires a
premium of Rs. 1,200 per family member per year. The
financial coverage provided is Rs. 2.00 lakhs per year for
each individual. The scheme includes 1,044 procedures
along with 138 follow-up packages, similar to those
offered under the Dr. NTR Vaidya Seva. Through Mee-
Seva, the Dr. NTR Vaidya Seva Health Scheme website, or
by contacting the designated agencies, Aarogya Raksha
can be enrolled. A total premium of Rs. 23.72 crores have
been collected, and payments have been settled for
20,618 claims, amounting to Rs. 40.57 crores.

## Amrutha Health Scheme for Orphans and destitute

Vide G.O.Ms. No.452 Revenue (CMRF) Department Dated:
16.07.2012,the united Govt of A.P have issued orders for
covering the Orphans and destitute in old age homes,

## ANDHRA PRADESH LEGISLATIVE ASSEMBLY SESSION-II LAQ No.187 (Starred) Notice given by Notice given by, Sri Bathula Balaramakrishna, MLA. Smt. Reddappa Gari Madhavi, MLA. Smt. Vemireddy Prashanthi Reddy, MLA. Will the Minister for Home and Disaster Management be pleased to state:- QUESTION: a. the number of cases of persons missing and trafficking of women registered between 2019-2024 in the state; the action to be taken by the government to prevent the trafficking of women and young Girls; and b. the action to be taken by the government to implement Friendly Policing effectively. ## Home (Arms) Department ANSWER **a).**Details of missing of persons from the year 2019 to 2024 up to October: Total 78189 missing persons were reported out of which 54122 are women and girls (below 18 years). Details of missing women during this period is given below.
Missing Cases
Year Female
(Including Girls
below 18 years)		 Girls
(Below 18 years)
2019-2024 (Oct) Total 54122 16366
Trafficking of Women from the year 2019 to 2024 up to October: 46 women victims of trafficking were identified during this period and 34 cases were registered. Action to be taken by the government to prevent the trafficking of women and young Girls: Formation of AHTUs in new Districts: • Currently, only 13 Anti-Human Trafficking Units (AHTUs) are established in the original 13 districts, in accordance with G.O.Ms.No.165, Home (PS & CA2) Dept., dated:25.06.2011 and G.O.Ms.No.47, Home (Services-III) Dept., dated:18.05.2021. Following the bifurcation of these 13 districts into 26 districts, 13 additional AHTUs will be established in the newly created districts to effectively combat human trafficking. (Continued...P.2)
